findings.issue: `subsample_indices` (and `_subsample` at :82) silently return the WHOLE pool when `n_train > n_pool` instead of failing. MNIST's train part is now 50,000, so the live sweep `for N in 2500 5000 10000 20000 40000 60000` (submit_fresh_suite.sh:108, submit_reruns_2026-09-17_part2.sh:30) trains the top point of `rebuttal_overparam_mnist_scan` on 50,000 examples while `result_id_fields: [mlp_width, n_data]` stamps `n_data=60000` into the run_id and the record. Verified on the real files: n_data=60000 -> n_train=50000. The overparam crossover figure's x axis (P/N) is then wrong by 20% for that point, and nothing anywhere fails or warns. Same silent cap for the synthetic classes: verified `Toy1DRegressionDataset(n_train=50000)` -> n_train=10000 and `RandomPolynomialDataset(n_train=50000)` -> 10000, so any future n_train above pool_size=10000 is quietly truncated. The implementer did flag the launcher consequence in their report, but the code-level guard that would make it non-silent is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: In `subsample_indices`, distinguish the two cases: return `arange(n_pool)` only for `n_train is None or n_train == n_pool`, and `raise ValueError(f"n_train={n_train} exceeds the pool of {n_pool}")` when `n_train > n_pool`. Alternatively (if a loud failure is unacceptable) store `self.n_train_requested` on every class so `_scan_facts` can record it and analysis can assert `n_train == n_data`. Either way the MNIST sweep must then be capped at 50000 in both launchers.

findings.issue: `split_seed` is not a uniform constructor argument: `MNISTDataset` (:136) and `CIFAR10Dataset` (:367) accept it, but `Toy1DRegressionDataset` (:96), `RandomPolynomialDataset` (:244), `CharTextDataset` (:408) and `TokenBinDataset` (:478) only *record* it and reject it as a kwarg. CONTRACTS.md's Datasets interface and WP-CFG both treat `split_seed` as a dataset-config value to be added across the 44 configs; the moment `split_seed: 1234` lands in a `dataset:` override block of a toy/polynomial/shakespeare/fineweb scan (or in those dataset yamls), Hydra instantiate raises `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'split_seed'` and every run of that scan dies at startup. Confirmed by signature inspection of all six classes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `split_seed=None` to all six signatures. Synthetic: `self.split_seed = int(seed if split_seed is None else split_seed)` and derive the three generator seeds from it (or from `seed`, but accept and record the argument). Text/token: accept it, record `int(split_seed)` if given else `None`. ~6 lines, keeps every current config working.

findings.issue: The script that produced F4 has zero test coverage. `write_split` is a closure inside `main()`, so it is not importable and cannot be unit-tested; the entire correctness argument is the one-off rebuild plus a manual `tools/check_token_split.py` run that nothing invokes automatically. The fix is literally one identifier away from the bug (`for ex in stream` at :48 vs the old `for ex in ds`), and a re-tokenisation or refactor by any later agent would re-contaminate the GPT-2 study silently. There is also no assertion that a split filled its budget: if the stream runs dry, `write_split` truncates to `n*2` and the following splits get 0 tokens, which makes `_BlockDataset.n` negative (`(0-1)//block_size = -1`) rather than raising.
findings.suggested_fix: Lift `write_split(stream, path, budget, encode, eot)` to module level and add a test in tests/test_datasets.py with a fake iterator of synthetic documents asserting (a) the documents landing in val, test and train are pairwise disjoint, (b) each file is exactly `n*2` bytes, (c) a stream that runs dry produces short-but-correct counts. Also raise (or at least print a loud WARNING) when `n < budget`, and guard `_BlockDataset` against an empty array.

findings.issue: `os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)` followed by `np.memmap(..., mode="w+")` overwrites an existing token directory with no confirmation. Re-running the invocation that is documented verbatim in the module docstring (:13-17) destroys the verified 500 MB `fineweb_edu_gpt2_v2/train.bin`, and pointing `--out` at the old directory destroys v1. In a working tree shared by ~10 agents, with the task carrying an explicit 'NEVER write into the old fineweb_edu_gpt2 directory' rule, that rule is enforced only by operator care.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--force` and refuse otherwise: `existing = [s for s in ("train","val","test") if os.path.exists(os.path.join(args.out, s + ".bin"))]` then `if existing and not args.force: sys.exit(f"refusing to overwrite {existing} in {args.out}; pass --force")`.

findings.issue: The block check samples 32 blocks of 256 tokens = 8,192 of 8,000,000 val tokens (0.1% coverage). It reliably catches the whole-file duplication of F4 (I confirmed v1 -> OVERLAP DETECTED, exit 1) but would very likely miss a partial contamination of, say, 1% of val. Separately, `trailing_zeros` (:75) is printed but never turned into a failure, so the 'unfilled file tail left as zeros' half of F4 does not fail the tool.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a document-level check that is both stronger and cheaper: split each array on `eot` (50256), hash each document (`hashlib.blake2b` over the bytes), and assert the three document-hash sets are pairwise disjoint; that catches any shared document, not a 0.1% sample. And make a trailing-zero run longer than, say, 1024 tokens a FAIL rather than a print.

findings.issue: `legacy_additive_powers` is not re-exported, although the report's 'New public API' section lists it among the helpers 'all exported from experiments.datasets'. tests/test_datasets.py:25 imports it from `experiments.datasets.all_datasets` directly so nothing breaks today, but an integrator following the report gets an ImportError.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `legacy_additive_powers` to the import list and `__all__`, or correct the report.

findings.issue: The file cannot be collected by a bare `pytest tests/test_datasets.py`: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'experiments'` (verified with `env -u PYTHONPATH .venv/bin/pytest`). It only works via `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` from the repo root or with `PYTHONPATH=$REPO`. There is no `conftest.py` in `tests/` or the repo root and no `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath` in pyproject.toml. This is repo-wide (every track's test file), and `campaign/run_cpu_tests.sh` does set PYTHONPATH, so it is only a trap for a hand-run `pytest tests/`.
findings.suggested_fix: Repo-level, not this track's file: add `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` with `pythonpath = ["."]` to pyproject.toml (or a two-line tests/conftest.py that inserts the repo root). Worth raising with the integrator so one track owns it.
